key_idea: A **pathogen** is a microorganism that causes disease. Pathogens are bacteria, viruses, fungi or protists. They spread by direct contact, in the air, in food and water, or on a vector, and each route can be blocked.

blocks.text: Some diseases can be passed from one organism to another. This section covers the four types of pathogen and how each one causes harm.

items.meaning: A disease caused by a pathogen that can be passed on, also called an infectious disease.
A disease that is not caused by a pathogen, so it is not passed from person to person.

rows: Reproduce rapidly in the body. May release **toxins** (poisons) that damage tissues and make you feel ill.
Live and reproduce inside cells. This damages the cells.
Infect plants or animals. Many spread as spores.
Rose black spot, barley powdery mildew
Single-celled organisms. Some live in a vector and pass to the host.

blocks.text: Pathogens may infect plants or animals. Bacteria and viruses can reproduce rapidly inside the body, so an infection can get worse quickly.

items: A pathogen is a microorganism that causes disease.
The four types are bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists.
Viruses damage the cells they live in. Bacteria can release toxins.

blocks.text: A pathogen has to get from one host to another. There are four main routes.

items: **Direct contact:** touching an infected person, or exchanging body fluids such as blood. HIV and Ebola spread this way.
**Air:** droplets from coughs and sneezes are breathed in. Measles and tuberculosis spread this way. Fungal spores can be carried by the wind.
**Food and water:** the pathogen is swallowed in food prepared in unhygienic conditions, or in dirty water. Salmonella and cholera spread this way.
**Vectors:** an organism that carries the pathogen from one host to another. Mosquitos spread malaria. Ticks spread Lyme disease.
Fungal spores are spread by wind and water, and enter leaves through the stomata.
Insects that feed on a plant can act as vectors. A virus in tulips is injected into the phloem by feeding insects.
Bacteria can be carried by beetles. In cucumber plants the bacteria block the xylem, so less water reaches the leaves and they wilt.

items: The four routes are direct contact, air, food and water, and vectors.
A vector is an organism that carries a pathogen between hosts.
Plant pathogens spread by wind, water and insects.

blocks.text: To stop a disease spreading, block the route it uses. Link each measure to the route it blocks.

items: **Air:** cover your nose and mouth when you cough or sneeze, avoid close contact with infected people, and isolate infected people.
**Food and water:** wash hands after using the toilet and before handling food, do not prepare food while infected, and do not share utensils or towels.
**Contact:** use a condom, do not share needles, and disinfect clothes and surfaces.
**Vectors:** use insecticides or remove breeding sites so there are fewer mosquitos. Use mosquito nets and repellents to avoid being bitten.
**Vaccination:** most people become immune, so fewer people are exposed to the pathogen. Chickens in the UK are vaccinated so fewer bacteria reach food.
Remove and burn infected plants. Clear dead plants from fields so spores do not spread to new plants.
Grow a different crop the next year. Spores left on barley cannot infect wheat, so the fungus dies out.
Spray insecticides to kill insect vectors.
Name the route, then give the measure that blocks it.
Vaccination means most of the population is immune, so there is less chance of a non-immune person meeting the pathogen.
Killing vectors and avoiding bites controls vector-borne disease.
